item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00359","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C06","C14"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.98,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 plausibly supplied a concrete and material template. It addresses the same Communications Act authorities, delegates emergency control over radio stations, authorizes implementing regulations, and contains distinctive limitations that reappear in the child. Most notably, both texts disclaim authority over station-program content, and both specifically address taking over stations and removing apparatus or equipment. The child broadens and reorganizes this machinery under the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. C06 is also closely related because it assigns telecommunications and section 305 frequency functions to the same Director, but it lacks the child's distinctive section 606 emergency-control machinery. C14 offers a weaker structural analogue involving delegated presidential powers whose exercise depends on a presidential wartime finding or proclamation.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the authority vested in the President by subsection 305 (a), and by subsections 606 (a), (c), and (d), of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended ... is delegated to the Director","parent_excerpt":"The authority vested in the President by section 606(c) of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, is hereby delegated to the Federal Communications Commission ... [and] pursuant to the authority vested in the President by section 305","explanation":"Both directives construct delegations under the same Communications Act provisions for governmental and nongovernmental radio-station control."},{"child_excerpt":"Nothing in this order shall be construed as authorizing the exercise of any authority with respect to the content of any station program","parent_excerpt":"Nothing in this order shall be construed as authorizing the Commission to exercise any authority with respect to the content of station programs.","explanation":"This is distinctive, nearly verbatim shared limiting language."},{"child_excerpt":"to take over or use facilities or stations or to remove apparatus or equipment from facilities or stations","parent_excerpt":"Nothing in this order shall be construed to authorize the Commission to take over and use any radio station or to remove the apparatus and equipment of any radio station.","explanation":"The child carries forward the same specific emergency-control acts while changing who may approve their exercise."},{"child_excerpt":"The Director may issue such rules and regulations as he may deem necessary in connection with the authority delegated to him","parent_excerpt":"The Federal Communications Commission ...
